cluster_summary: The cluster consists of vulnerabilities where tool authorization policies are bypassed due to insufficient identity validation, missing allowlists, and lack of authentication checks, alongside sensitive data exposure through insecure logging and parameter passing. These issues stem from assuming input trustworthiness and failing to enforce consistent security boundaries across tool loading, policy enforcement, and output handling.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Require explicit type prefixes in policy keys or cross-validate identity from multiple sources (raw input, metadata, title) and fail closed if any conflict arises..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: Identifier collision and cross-validation gaps
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Require explicit type prefixes in policy keys or cross-validate identity from multiple sources (raw input, metadata, title) and fail closed if any conflict arises.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Require explicit type prefixes in policy keys or cross-validate identity from multiple sources (raw input, metadata, title) and fail closed if any conflict arises.
sub_patterns.name: Identifier collision and cross-validation gaps
sub_patterns.root_cause: Authorization logic uses a single identifier (e.g., ID, username, display name) without disambiguating types or cross-validating against multiple identity sources, allowing attackers to spoof identities or collide with privileged users.
